metadata.note: CLI explainer (cli-explainer skill — ADVANCED tier), built on D:\ai1-cli-main per CLAUDE.md rule 3. Folder dated 2026-09-22 per explicit instruction. Follows the mandatory CLI spine with one revision cycle (THE REVISION LAW satisfied). ACTUAL-CODE LAW: code/ holds four REAL runnable scripts (corpus.py, encoder.py, pipeline.py, diagnose.py); both CODE beats quote them verbatim and every number on screen is captured stdout, saved as _run-pipeline.txt and _run-diagnose.txt. Retrieval is REAL all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (encoder.py carried over from the Chapter 6 reel — same hand-rolled safetensors loader and numpy BERT forward pass, since sentence-transformers is absent here). THE GENERATE STAGE IS NOT AN LLM and the reel says so out loud: it is a deterministic extractive reader that can only quote a sentence physically present in the prompt's CONTEXT block. That is a deliberate CONTROL, not a shortcut — a stochastic LLM could mask a retrieval fault by guessing correctly from prior knowledge, which would destroy the very stage-localisation this chapter is about. B01/B09 reuse RagExecutiveSummary and B08 reuses CliRunOutput, props-only. B04/B07 are two new bespoke components (PipelineTrace, FaultSignatureTable) — GATE L searched four ways; the closest lead, HaiBrutalistE01Pipeline, hardcodes its stage list as a module constant and exposes only sparkLine. B11 is TitleOutroChannel per OUTRO-LOCK.md §Scope.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — the ask lands answered.
beats.narration_text: Vanakkam — I'm Vedanshu Daxesh Patel. Four chapters have built four pieces: representation, chunking, indexing, retrieval. None of them, on its own, is RAG. Chapter seven bolts them together and runs one question all the way through — and then asks the question that actually matters in production: when the answer is wrong, which piece broke?

beats.role_note: Mandatory PROBLEM beat: the stakes, stated BEFORE any prompt.
beats.narration_text: Here is the problem, before we write a line. A finished RAG system gives you one output: an answer. When that answer is wrong, you have one symptom and four suspects. The pipeline's real value is not that it runs — it is that it has named seams, so a symptom at the end can be traced back to exactly one place where something specific went wrong.

show.event: Headline types in: 'One symptom. Four suspects.'
Subline resolves: named seams are what make a bug locatable
Spark line settles

props.headline: One symptom. Four suspects.
props.subline: A finished pipeline emits a single answer, so a wrong answer looks the same whatever caused it. Naming the seams is what turns one symptom back into one stage.

beats.narration_text: The ask: five stages, five functions, one return value each. Ingest turns documents into chunks. Embed turns chunks into vectors. Retrieve turns a question into a short list. Augment turns that list into a prompt. Generate turns the prompt into an answer. And print what each stage hands to the next — because if I can't print the handoffs, the seams aren't real.

show.event: Spark greeting 'The ask,' holds
Command types — five functions, and print every handoff
Send arms; runningText 'generating pipeline…'

beats.narration_text: Read the shape, not the detail. Five functions. Ingest takes documents and returns chunks. Embed takes chunks and returns an index. Retrieve takes a question and returns a list. Augment takes that list and returns a string. Generate takes the string and returns an answer. Nothing reaches past its neighbour — and that discipline is the whole reason the next cycle works.

beats.narration_text: Run it. Six documents become thirteen chunks. Thirteen chunks become a thirteen-by-three-eighty-four index. The question retrieves three chunks — all three from the vacation policy, because paragraphs of the same document sit close together. Those become a six-hundred-and-fifteen character prompt. And out falls: first-year employees accrue twelve paid vacation days, cited to V-A-one-oh-one.

beats.role_note: THE REVISION LAW — the second cycle begins here.
beats.narration_text: Now the revision, and this is the part the chapter is really about. Break exactly one stage at a time. Hold everything else identical. Then record three things: did the right fact come back, did it cite anything, and was the answer even present in the prompt. If the three faults produce three different signatures, the pipeline is a diagnostic map. If any two look the same, it is decoration.

props.segment: Watch A Bug Name Its Own Stage.
props.command: claude "now write diagnose.py — break exactly ONE stage at a time (retrieve, augment, generate), hold the rest identical, and record three signals per run: did the right fact come back, what did it cite, was the answer grounded in the prompt. Report whether the signatures differ."

beats.narration_text: Three faults, each a single switch. Retrieve gets a filter bug that skips the right document entirely. Augment drops the chunk labels, so the context arrives unlabelled. Generate ignores the context and answers from a prior — the hallucination case. One trace function runs all three through the same pipeline and records what came back.

trace() — one switch per stage, everything else held constant
spark line settles: one switch per stage

props.title: diagnose.py — one fault at a time

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the chapter's diagnostic claim, tested. Real data from _run-diagnose.txt.
beats.narration_text: And the claim holds. Break retrieve: a real chunk comes back, correctly cited, grounded in the prompt — and it is about sick days. Break augment: the right fact comes back, grounded, citing nothing. Break generate: no fact, no citation, not grounded at all. Three faults. Three different signatures. Not one of them looks like another.

beats.narration_text: And this is what makes it land. Read what the broken retriever returned: employees receive ten paid sick days per calendar year. Fluent. Correctly cited. Completely irrelevant. That is the failure mode nobody catches by reading answers — it looks like a good answer to a question nobody asked.

beats.role_note: Mandatory SUMMARY beat — the lesson, plus what this build does NOT prove.
beats.narration_text: So: five stages, five seams, and a symptom that points at exactly one of them. One honest limit, though. My generator is not a language model — it is a deterministic reader that can only quote the prompt. That is the reason the signatures came out this clean. A real model can guess right from prior knowledge and hide a retrieval fault, or guess wrong and imitate one. The map still works. It just gets harder to read.

props.headline: The seams are the instrument.
props.subline: Five stages that each hand on exactly one thing are what let a single wrong answer be traced back to a single place — and a deterministic reader is what makes that trace legible.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: 'Take my RAG system and log, for every answer it gives, three things — which chunks were retrieved, whether the answer text appears in those chunks, and what it cited. Then show me the answers where those three disagree.' That last sentence is the whole trick. You are not asking for an accuracy score; you are asking for the rows where the pipeline contradicts itself, because those are the ones where a stage is broken and the answer still looked fine.
